### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. ovarian cancer  —  Tier 2 — Strong / Probable  (fitness 0.619)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-1250342, Reactome:R-HSA-202424, Reactome:R-HSA-2219530, Reactome:R-HSA-2424491, Reactome:R-HSA-5655302)

**Proposed mechanism:** PIK3CA (HGNC:9537) —INCREASES→ PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (WP:WP449); AKT1 (HGNC:391) —INCREASES→ PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (WP:WP449); PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (WP:WP449) —LEADS_TO→ Hemifacial myohyperplasia (MONDO:0011723); PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (WP:WP449) —LEADS_TO→ Ovarian cancer (MONDO:0008170). Gain-of-function mutations in PIK3CA and AKT1 lead to aberrant activation of the PI3K-Akt signaling pathway. This dysregulated pathway drives cellular proliferation and survival, contributing to the development of hemifacial myohyperplasia and ovarian cancer.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of activating mutations in PIK3CA or AKT1 in a significant proportion of patients with either hemifacial myohyperplasia or ovarian cancer would challenge this hypothesis. _(variant: rs767715110 (PIK3CA E545K) with a gnomAD allele frequency > 1% in relevant populations.)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the PI3K-Akt pathway is a promising therapeutic strategy for both conditions, with existing PI3K inhibitors showing efficacy in ovarian cancer and potential for application in other hyperplastic disorders.

#### 2. megalencephaly-capillary malformation-polymicrogyria syndrome  —  Tier 2 — Strong / Probable  (fitness 0.602)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-1250342, Reactome:R-HSA-202424, Reactome:R-HSA-2219530, Reactome:R-HSA-2424491, Reactome:R-HSA-5655302)

**Proposed mechanism:** PIK3CA (HGNC:9533) —DISRUPTS→ PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP1080); PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP1080) —INCREASES→ Abnormal cell growth and proliferation (HP:0001575); PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP1080) —INCREASES→ Abnormal brain development (HP:0011190); Abnormal cell growth and proliferation (HP:0001575) —LEADS_TO→ Hemifacial myohyperplasia (MONDO:0011723); Abnormal brain development (HP:0011190) —LEADS_TO→ Megalencephaly-capillary malformation-polymicrogyria syndrome (MONDO:0011240). Gain-of-function mutations in PIK3CA lead to aberrant activation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway. This dysregulated pathway promotes abnormal cell growth and proliferation, contributing to the phenotype of hemifacial myohyperplasia. Concurrently, the same pathway dysregulation impacts abnormal brain development, manifesting as megalencephaly-capillary malformation-polymicrogyria syndrome.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in PIK3CA associated with hemifacial myohyperplasia that do not lead to increased PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling, or identification of individuals with megalencephaly-capillary malformation-polymicrogyria syndrome caused by mutations in genes entirely separate from the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway. _(variant: rs373719959)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway could offer a therapeutic strategy for both hemifacial myohyperplasia and megalencephaly-capillary malformation-polymicrogyria syndrome, given the shared genetic basis and mechanistic overlap.
